newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares finish lower, ITC slides 9 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares finish lower, ITC slides 9 percent.

text.p: A small rally towards the close of trade saw blue-chip stocks end with minor losses on Wednesday, dealers said.
Market activity was generally sluggish with action focussed on ITC shares which crashed 24.75 rupees or 9.2 percent to close at 244.0 rupees at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
Traders said there was little interest in the market as participants tracked the Titan Cup final being played between India and South Africa in Bombay.
"The cricket match is drawing a lot of interest from fund managers and traders," a dealer said.
Speculators were heavy sellers in ITC, traders said. The firm is being investigated by a federal agency for alleged violations of foreign exchange rules involving over $100 million.
Indian finance firms and B.A.T. Industries Plc, which together control nearly 70 percent of ITC equity, said on Tuesday they would review operations at the troubled firm on November 15.
A B.A.T. spokesman in London said, "This is a very valuable investment...there is no change to our investment view of ITC."
A Delhi court on Wednesday granted bail to former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, hours after he was formally charged in a 1983 cheating case, court officials said.

EIH (formerly East India Hotels Ltd) announced a 19 percent rise in its first-half 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 474.3 million rupees against 399.0 million rupees in the same period a year ago. Shares of EIH lost 1.75 rupees to 362.0 at the BSE.
ACC fell 12.0 to 1,418.0, SBI 1.0 to 214.0 and Bajaj Auto 8.50 to 917.0. TISCO rose 0.25 to 165.75, BSES 1.25 to 188.25 and TELCO 3.25 to 399.0. Reliance was unchanged at 185.0.
